items_missed: No agenda statement or explicit 'sound good?' confirmation before jumping into move details and pricing
Didn't ask about additional rooms, narrow hallways/tight turns, access/parking or HOA concerns at either stop, or ask about moving stressors
No 'pricing is super simple' opener and no detailed breakdown of what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, tools)
Never mentioned the No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) — a missed opportunity given the customer flagged a ~500lb vintage cast-iron stove
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch (fuel surcharge, assembly fees, credit card fees) — only a passing 'no trip fees' and, when asked, 'no deposits or credit card info'
Didn't explain when the clock starts on-site, the 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum, or do a sense-check ('does that make sense?')
Never stated the explicit number of movers being sent (implied by the math, but not said aloud)
Didn't address drive time between the two stops (house then apartment ~2 miles away) or ask about walk distance from truck to door
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no consolidation tips, no 'take a carload' suggestion, no shorter-move-lower-bill framing
Didn't ask 'any other questions before I let you go?' or give hours/how to reach the company
Only used the customer's name once ('Stacy') near the very end, despite learning it — did not hit 3+ name uses
No insurance explanation (No Worries Damage / 60 cents per lb) despite the customer volunteering a valuable vintage item
top_strength: Sergio quickly nailed down the job scope (truck size, item list, two drop-off stops, no stairs) and gave a clear, itemized hourly price with a specific dollar range and start time, moving the customer to a booked slot in under 7 minutes.
coaching_note: Sergio should open with a stated agenda and a 'sound good?' check-in, and should not skip No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, the On-Time Guarantee, and the Save Your Ass prep speech — this call in particular handed him a natural lead-in (the customer's ~500lb vintage stove) to pitch damage protection and he let it pass.
phone_presence_notes: Sergio is polite and casually friendly throughout ('Cool,' 'awesome sauce,' 'perfect') and the customer stayed positive and thanked him by name at the close, but there are no explicit empathy statements, humor, or acknowledgment of the customer's stove concern beyond a flat 'gotcha.'
